title: Credibility assessment of CFD models for an intravascular catheter: trackability and flow resistance under ASME V&V 40
runhead: CFD credibility for catheter trackability and resistance
device: Steerable intravascular catheter intended for coronary and peripheral arterial navigation

models.name: Model A: Lumen Flow CFD
models.what_it_computes: Steady, incompressible Navier–Stokes solution inside the catheter lumen to predict pressure drop, wall shear stress, and flow partitioning with and without a guidewire present.

models.name: Model B: External Flow CFD with Imposed Advancement
models.what_it_computes: Transient, pulsatile external flow around the catheter within an idealized vessel curve with prescribed catheter advancement; computes surface shear/pressure distributions, net lateral tip force, and unsteady drag.

mechanisms.name: M1: Lumen pressure drop at clinical infusion rates
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines flow resistance, informing maximum deliverable flow rate and label claims for infusion and contrast delivery.

mechanisms.name: M2: Outer-surface shear and drag during advancement
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Contributes to the force required to track the catheter through tortuous vessels and affects controllability during navigation.

mechanisms.name: M3: Lateral tip force from asymmetric outlet geometry
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Side holes and bevels can induce cross-stream forces that bias steering and affect trackability around bends.

mechanisms.name: M4: Flow-induced distal shaft oscillations
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady hydrodynamic loading can promote tip oscillation that degrades control and may elevate local vessel wall stresses.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Index, assigned separately for each (model × mechanism) pair.
